title: Dunholm Research: TrialVault
description: A Durham-based clinical research startup is under external audit after a competitor published three paragraphs of the NIMMOD-2 Phase 2 dossier verbatim. Players act as the external auditor and chain six weaknesses through the TrialVault platform: unauthenticated Spring Boot Actuator exposure, directory traversal through a filter-strip sanitiser, JWT algorithm confusion via a trust-alg-header verifier, blind boolean SQL injection on a raw-concat search endpoint, RSA-512 + AES-256-GCM hybrid decryption combining per-user and shared key material, and plaintext credential leak through DEBUG request-body logging.
learningObjectives: Recognise unrestricted Spring Boot Actuator exposure as a production-grade misconfiguration and understand the differing blast radius of env, info, and logfile
Identify filter-strip traversal patterns that survive naive replace("../", "") sanitisation and reason about the interaction between Spring URL decoding and filter order
Understand why trusting the alg header of an incoming JWT is equivalent to leaking the signing key, and reproduce the public-key-as-HMAC-secret forgery
Walk a full boolean blind SQL injection end to end against a single count-returning endpoint, including extraction length and characterwise probing with Hibernate JDBC-escape-syntax awareness
Combine an asymmetric weakness (short RSA modulus) with a symmetric recovery path (shared-secret composition) and observe that each half alone is insufficient
Recognise that DEBUG request-body logging in production is an A09 finding that yields credentials directly, not a privacy oversight
Map vulnerabilities to OWASP A01, A02, A03, A05, A07, A09 (2021)
